correctness.rationale: For each target vertex there are two possible predecessors or no selected incoming arc. Exhausting these 3^7 choices and removing vertices of indegree zero until no more can be removed independently recovers the complete augmented face counts (1,14,84,280,553,616,301). The specified seven +1 then seven +2 pivots give disjoint face pairs at each pivot and 910 pairs in total. Reversing the matched covering incidences produces a Hasse digraph whose topological traversal visits all 1849 vertices, with 29 unmatched faces, all of cardinality six. On removing the empty face from the matching, its formerly paired vertex is the only critical 0-cell; the 29 critical 5-cells attach to that point in the Morse CW model, proving the wedge. Any nonidentity translation has order seven and its two arc orbits are Hamiltonian directed cycles; no nonempty admissible face is stabilized and a fixed point would stabilize its supporting face. Hence the quotient is a free seven-sheeted covering with simply connected total space and deck group C₇. Cartan–Leray in total degree ≤4 has only the bottom row, with no differential to the cover's first nonzero positive row at degree 5 in that range; the period-two cyclic resolution gives Z/7 in degrees 1 and 3 and zero in 2 and 4. Top homology is free since the quotient is five-dimensional CW; χ=(1−29)/7=−4 gives rank five. Independent signed orbit-cell boundaries give cell counts (2,12,40,79,88,43), d²=0, and exact Smith torsion [none,7,none,7,none,none] for homology: the image of the next boundary is in the kernel of the current one, and the image of the current boundary is free, so the torsion of its degree's incoming cokernel is exactly homology torsion. For the rational cover module, trivial Lefschetz number at nonidentity elements forces trace one in odd degree five, compared to 29 at the identity; this is exactly the rational character Q⊕4Q[C₇]. No integral representation splitting or quotient homotopy model is asserted.

value.rationale: The full next-neighbor orbit on the seven-cycle gives a natural sparse 2-out Cayley digraph beyond tournament examples, not an arbitrary selection of shortcuts. Its exact 29-sphere cover and signed cyclic quotient data provide a positive benchmark in which a nontrivial free action on a highly connected directed-forest complex produces torsion in two quotient degrees. The exact benchmark, rather than novelty of the standard spectral-sequence inference or any generalization in the prime, is the useful mathematical contribution.
